items.title: The dispatcher's fold push takes the ship lock too
items.description:
## What happens today

ISS-333 (3.35.181) made the ship take `.git/forge-ship-lock` around its fetch, rebase, gate, version and push, so two ships on one checkout land one at a time. The dispatcher's fold does not go through the ship: it commits the dry-run journal entry in the shared checkout and pushes it with `git fetch && git rebase origin/master && git push origin HEAD:master`. That push takes no lock, so it can land between a ship's rebase and its push. It did, on the lock's own first outing: run 164's journal commit (c8771d6) beat ISS-333's ship at step 6, the push was rejected, and the run resumed with `--from 2` (ISS-333's landing account, comment of 07:45, corrected at 07:51).

## Outcome

A fold's landing honours the same lock a ship's landing does. Either `tools/run.mjs` gains a verb for landing a commit that is not a release (take the lock, fetch, rebase, push, release — no gate, no version), or the lock is exposed so a caller can hold it around its own push. The dispatch guide's fold step names that route in place of the bare rebase-and-push line, and a push from the shared checkout while a ship holds the lock is what the guide tells a dispatcher not to do.

## Rules

- The lock is one file and one rule; the fold does not grow a second lock or a second contention message.
- A fold blocked by a held lock waits for the ship's release rather than failing — a fold has nothing to unwind.
- The lock's holder record names the tree that holds it, so a dispatcher can see which run it waits on.

## Out of scope

- Commits made by hand outside both the ship and the fold.
- Changing what the ship does while it holds the lock.

## Where

`tools/run.mjs`, `tools/run/lock.mjs`, `plugin/guides/skills/dispatch/guide.md`.

## Why

The rejected push costs a run one resume: a second fetch, a second rebase, and a second gate of several minutes. The profiler's `ships` line counts these; the parent's own pushes are one of the causes it cannot see.
items.plan:
# Plan — the fold's landing takes the ship's lock, through a verb of its own

Screen change: no
Schema coupling: no
User-facing outcome: no

## The one thing verified in code that makes this possible

`lockFile()` in `tools/run/lock.mjs` resolves through `gitCommonDir()`, never
`--absolute-git-dir`, so the shared checkout and every `wt-ISS-*` worktree contend on one file,
`<common>/forge-ship-lock`. `plugin/test/run/run-lock.test.mjs` asserts that equality directly. A
push made from the checkout root under `takeShipLock` therefore serializes against a worktree's
ship with no new mechanism at all — the lock already spans the pair, it was simply never taken by
anything but `ship`.

## Correction to the issue's premise

The issue asks that the dispatch guide's fold step name the locked route "in place of the bare
rebase-and-push line". That line is not in the guide: `plugin/guides/skills/dispatch/guide.md` and
`references/the-fold.md` contain neither the word `push` nor `rebase`. The bare command was the
dispatcher's own habit, unwritten. So the fold reference *gains* the rule rather than replacing a
line.

The issue's third rule — "the lock's holder record names the tree that holds it" — is already met:
`shipHolder()` returns `{ tree, branch }` and `whose()` prints both. No code is owed for it; the
criteria judge it as standing behaviour.

## Before and after

**Before.** `node tools/run.mjs` has three verbs. `start` cuts a worktree, `ship` runs ten steps and
holds the lock from the fetch to the push, `review` moves a mark. Nothing lands a commit that is not
a release, so the dispatcher's journal commit reaches `master` by a bare `git fetch && git rebase &&
git push` from the shared checkout, which can land between a ship's rebase and its push and did
(run 164's `c8771d6` against ISS-333's own first ship).

**After.** A fourth verb, `land`, lands one commit that is not a release: four steps — the tree is
clean, fetch, rebase, push — of which the last three are the locked span, dropped at the push. The
clean check is outside it, where the ship's own step 1 already is: a tree nobody can rebase is
refused before the branch is held rather than after, and the lock is taken only by a run that will
reach a push. No gate, no version bump, no install steps, no `forge-ship-from` mark, no review
count. A fold behind a held lock prints whose landing it waits on and waits for the release, as a
ship does.

## What `land` is, and what its three guards are not

`land` spends no gate, so what it pushes is the caller's judgement and not this script's. It is the
route for a commit a release would be wrong for — the wave journal the fold writes — and it is
stated that way in the help, because a verb that looked like a checked route would be one somebody
lands code through.

Its guards close the mis-invocation the shape invites, and none is a claim about the content: a run
typing `land` in its own worktree instead of `ship`. They are that this tree is the checkout itself,
that its HEAD is on the default branch, and that nothing is uncommitted — the three things true of
the shared checkout the fold commits in, and the second is what stops a checkout parked on somebody's
branch from pushing it. All three run before the lock is taken, so a refused `land` never held the
branch. A clean code commit sitting on the checkout's own default branch passes all three and is
landed ungated; that is the route working as intended, and the help says so rather than implying a
check.

## Files

- **`tools/run/args.mjs`** — a `land` entry in `VERBS`: signature `land [--wait M]`, the one flag,
  no bare words. `flagLines` dedupes by flag name, because `usage()` flattens every verb's flags
  into one list and `--wait` would otherwise print twice.
- **`tools/run.mjs`** — `landSteps(tree, base)` returning the four steps, the last three carrying
  the ship's own `LANDS`/`PUSHES` roles, and `land({ flags })` running them under `takeShipLock`
  with the same `--wait` reading `ship` does, after the guards. `usage()` gains `land`'s signature, its lines and the sentences saying it lands what is
  not a release and spends no gate; the first line becomes `<start|ship|land|review>`; `VERB_RUNS`
  and the unknown-verb refusal name it. `cleanTree`'s refusal says "a landing pushes commits" rather
  than "a release ships commits", one message serving both callers.
- **`tools/run/lock.mjs`** — `staleSaid` and `wedgedSaid` say *landing* where they said *ship*, and
  the stale escape says to run the landing again rather than to ship again. One lock, one contention
  message, true for either caller. No new export and no second lock.
- **`plugin/guides/skills/dispatch/guide.md`, `references/the-fold.md`** — the fold's own landing
  goes through the project's landing route, which serializes with the runs' landings; a push made
  from the shared checkout while a run is landing is what a dispatcher does not do. Stated as
  method: no path and no verb name, because this guide travels to every project that installs the
  plugin and the project's own record is where its route is named.
- **`plugin/test/run/run-lock.test.mjs`** — cases for the span: a `land` behind a held lock names the
  holder, waits, and against a fixture whose remote nobody else moves reaches no push and leaves that
  holder's lock in place; `land` spends no gate and makes no version commit; a `land` from a
  worktree, from a branch that is not the default, and on a dirty tree are each refused, take no lock
  and leave none behind.
- **`plugin/test/run/run-script.test.mjs`** — the `-h` case grows to four verbs and asserts `land`'s
  signature; a `land -h` reaches no step, as `ship -h` does.

## What this deliberately does not change

- What the ship does while it holds the lock: the same span, the same steps, the same order.
- The lock's file, its acquire loop, its wait, its stale and wedged refusals as *rules* — only the
  noun in two sentences.
- Commits made by hand outside both the ship and the fold: past its three guards `land` judges nothing
  about what it is asked to push, and no gate stands between that commit and the branch.
- `tools/gates/steps.mjs`: the `test` step already declares `tools` and `plugin`, so both changed
  trees are inside a step that runs.
- The project brief: its landing line already ends by pointing at `node tools/run.mjs -h`, which
  will name `land`.

## Documented convention reversed

None. `docs/` names no verb table for this script — `node tools/run.mjs -h` is its whole surface, and
that is what this change rewrites.
items.acceptanceCriteria:
1. `node tools/run.mjs land` lands the checkout's HEAD on the default branch by fetch, rebase and push.
2. BR-06~1: `land` holds the same `forge-ship-lock` file the ship holds, across its fetch, its rebase and its push.
3. A `land` that meets a lock held by a running ship names the tree holding it.
4. That `land` waits for the lock's release rather than refusing at once.
5. A `land` that waits out its ceiling makes no push of its own.
6. A ship that meets a lock a `land` holds waits behind it rather than racing it.
7. That waiting ship prints the same contention sentence a waiting `land` prints.
8. `land` runs the project's gate at no point.
9. `land` makes no version commit of its own.
10. `land` runs no install step: neither the marketplace update nor the plugin update.
11. `land` from a tree that is not the checkout itself is refused.
12. That refusal names the route a worktree takes instead.
13. `land` from a HEAD that is not on the default branch is refused.
14. That refusal names the branch it found.
15. `land` on a tree with uncommitted work is refused.
16. That refusal lists the uncommitted paths.
17. A `land` its own guards refuse takes no lock, so none is left behind.
18. A `land` that waits out its ceiling leaves the holder's lock exactly where it was.
19. `node tools/run.mjs -h` names `land` with its signature.
20. That same usage says `land` lands a commit that is not a release.
21. That same usage says `land` spends no gate.
22. `node tools/run.mjs land -h` prints `land`'s own arguments.
23. `node tools/run.mjs land -h` reaches no step.
24. The usage prints one line per flag name, so a flag two verbs share is listed once.
25. The stale-lock refusal names a landing rather than a ship.
26. The wedged-lock refusal names a landing rather than a ship.
27. The stale-lock refusal's escape is a command a dispatcher folding a wave can act on.
28. `tools/run/lock.mjs` names exactly one lock file after the change, as it did before it.
29. `tools/run/lock.mjs` carries exactly one contention message after the change, as it did before it.
30. The lock's holder record names the tree holding it.
31. A run waiting behind a lock prints that tree.
32. `forge guide dispatch the-fold` tells a dispatcher that the fold's own landing goes through the project's landing route rather than a bare push from the shared checkout.
33. That guide text names no path, no script and no verb of this repository.
34. `npm run check` is green on the branch at the head that lands.

items.title: forge new --into still demands --title, though its own usage says a comment needs none
items.description:
## What happened

`forge new <file> --into ISS-27` is refused with "An issue needs --title; the tracker refuses an
untitled one", although both the usage line and the guide say `--into` comments on that issue
instead of filing and "needs none".

`plugin/src/commands.mjs:333` runs the title check before the route is chosen:

```
const { into, with: rides, size, kind, priority, new: fresh, ...given } = flags(rest, "new", ["--new"]);
if (!given.title) fail("An issue needs --title; the tracker refuses an untitled one.");
```

`commenting` is decided twelve lines further down (`const commenting = into !== undefined;`), so the
refusal that belongs to a filing is spoken over a comment. Seen at 3.35.183 while routing a finding
out of ISS-506, which is the route the issue-flow guide gives for a finding that belongs to another
issue: "`forge new --into`, which takes no lease".

## Outcome

`forge new <file> --into ISS-45` posts the comment with no `--title`, as its own usage says. A run
that has a finding for another issue types the one command the guide names and it works, rather
than inventing a title the comment does not use.

## Rules

- The check stays where a filing is made: an issue with no `--into` is still refused without a
  title, and its message does not change.
- The fix is one move of an existing check, not a new flag or a new message.

## Out of scope

Every other refusal of `new`, and what `--into` does once it is past this one.

## Where

`plugin/src/commands.mjs:333`, against the usage at `NEW_USAGE` in the same tree.

## Where

- forge 3.35.183 at /run/media/thanh/New/ai-project/wt-ISS-506/plugin
- met from project forge-plugin (.forge.json), prose as written
- agent claude-code_2-1-258_agent, in /run/media/thanh/New/ai-project/wt-ISS-506
